title: EKSU MCB 409 - Pathogenic Mycology (MCB 409) | Practice Bank

questions.stem: Which of the following is a primary mechanism by which fungal pathogens overcome the host's innate immune system, beyond simple evasion?

options.A: Rapid replication to overwhelm phagocytic cells.
options.B: Production of toxins that directly lyse immune cells.
options.C: Formation of biofilms that shield them from immune surveillance.
options.D: Mimicry of host cell surface molecules to avoid recognition.

questions.stem: A patient presents with a widespread fungal infection that originated from an inhaled spore. This type of mycosis is most accurately classified as:
Dimorphism in pathogenic fungi is a critical factor in their pathogenicity because it allows them to:

options.A: Produce a wider array of extracellular enzymes.
options.B: Adapt to different host environments, such as tissue invasion.
options.D: Increase their sporulation rate within the host.

questions.stem: The collection of a blood sample for fungal culture requires specific aseptic techniques primarily to:

options.A: Prevent contamination by commensal skin fungi.
options.B: Ensure the viability of fastidious fungal species.
options.C: Minimize the risk of iatrogenic fungal transmission.
options.D: Facilitate rapid identification of fungal elements.

questions.stem: Which of the following predisposing conditions to fungal infections is characterized by a disruption of the normal microbial flora?
The ability of a fungus to tolerate physiological temperatures found within the human body is a direct contribution to its pathogenicity by enabling:

options.B: Efficient nutrient acquisition from host tissues.
options.C: Survival and proliferation within the host.

questions.stem: Processing an ear exudate for fungal isolation would typically involve:

options.A: Direct microscopic examination with KOH and culture on Sabouraud's agar.
options.B: Gram staining and subsequent bacterial culture.
options.C: Acid-fast staining to rule out mycobacterial co-infection.

questions.stem: A patient with advanced HIV infection develops a fungal infection in the lungs that spreads to the brain. This is a classic example of:

options.D: Spreading the infection to the other eye.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a common predisposing factor for fungal infections?

options.B: Changes in ambient temperature and CO2 levels.
options.C: The presence of specific bacterial co-infections.
options.D: Depletion of essential trace elements in the environment.

questions.stem: When processing sputum for fungal culture, it is crucial to:

options.A: Use a sterile saline solution to dilute the sample.
options.B: Induce liquefaction of the mucus to release fungal elements.
options.C: Stain the sample directly with Gram stain.
options.D: Filter the sample to remove particulate matter.

questions.stem: A subcutaneous mycosis, such as sporotrichosis, is typically acquired through:

options.C: Direct inoculation of the fungus into the dermis.

questions.stem: The evasion of host defenses by pathogenic fungi can involve mechanisms such as:

options.B: Mimicry of host cell surface receptors.
options.C: Formation of a thick, resistant capsule.

questions.stem: The processing of hair for dermatophyte detection often involves:

options.A: Direct microscopic examination with India ink.
options.C: Treatment with chloral hydrate or KOH for visualization.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key characteristic of superficial mycoses?

options.B: They are confined to the outermost layers of the skin, hair, and nails.
options.C: They require immunosuppression for infection to occur.
options.D: They are primarily caused by dimorphic fungi.

questions.stem: The ability of some fungi to produce melanin is a pathogenicity factor that contributes to:

options.B: Resistance to oxidative stress and phagocytosis.
options.C: Efficient nutrient scavenging from host tissues.

questions.stem: A patient presents with a localized infection following a thorn prick, characterized by a granulomatous lesion that has spread along lymphatic vessels. This clinical presentation is most suggestive of:

The presence of a capsule in some pathogenic yeasts, such as Cryptococcus neoformans, is a significant virulence factor because it:

options.D: Enhances the production of hydrolytic enzymes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common predisposing factor for candidiasis, an opportunistic mycosis?

options.A: High dietary intake of vitamin D.

questions.stem: The enzymatic activity of fungal pathogens, such as the production of elastase, contributes to pathogenicity by:

options.D: Promoting fungal adhesion to host surfaces.

questions.stem: When collecting a sample for suspected tinea capitis (ringworm of the scalp), the most appropriate method for obtaining diagnostic material is:

options.A: Swabbing the affected area with a sterile cotton swab.
options.B: Scraping scales from the periphery of lesions and plucking affected hairs.
options.C: Collecting a biopsy of the affected scalp tissue.
options.D: Obtaining a sample of cerebrospinal fluid.

options.C: Inhibit the activity of host proteases.
options.D: Facilitate the breakdown of host collagen.

options.B: Incubation in a selective broth medium followed by subculture.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of opportunistic mycoses?

options.A: They are exclusively caused by highly virulent fungi.
options.B: They occur in individuals with compromised immune systems or disrupted normal flora.
options.C: They are always acquired through inhalation.
options.D: They are typically confined to the skin.

options.D: Add a preservative to the sample before transport.

questions.stem: The phenomenon of fungal dimorphism is most critically important for pathogenicity in which of the following scenarios?

options.A: Survival in the soil as a saprophyte.
options.B: Initial colonization of the skin surface.
options.C: Invasion of deep tissues and organs.
options.D: Dispersal of spores in the environment.

questions.stem: Processing sputum for fungal culture requires special attention to remove excessive mucus to:

options.B: Improve the visibility of fungal elements.
options.C: Enhance the growth of fastidious fungi.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common predisposing factor for mucormycosis, a rapidly progressive opportunistic mycosis?
The presence of a capsule in *Cryptococcus neoformans* is a significant virulence factor that primarily contributes to:

options.C: Inhibition of phagocytosis and complement-mediated lysis.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical samples is most appropriate for diagnosing a fungal infection of the nails (onychomycosis)?

options.A: A swab of the nail surface.
options.B: A biopsy of the nail bed.
options.C: Deeper nail clippings and debris from under the nail.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of systemic mycoses?
